newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: French film producer's wife found dead in Ireland.
newsitem.headline: French film producer's wife found dead in Ireland.

text.p: The wife of French film producer and critic Daniel Toscan du Plantier has been found battered to death on a remote country road in Ireland, Irish police said on Tuesday.
They said that the partially-clothed body of Sophie Toscan du Plantier, 38, from Ambrax, near Paris was discovered in the village of Schull in County Cork, south-west Ireland.
Police said she had suffered severe head injuries and they were hunting the killer.
Irish police said the woman had a holiday home in the area and had arrived in Ireland late last week to spend Christmas there.
Her car was still parked outside her cottage on Tuesday and there was no sign of a break-in.
The victim's husband, Daniel Toscan du Plantier, produces and promotes French films and is a familiar figure at the Cannes film festival.
Spokeswomen for his companies Unifrance and Erato Films said he was on holiday in south-western France and had been informed of the murder.
"Mr Toscan du Plantier just called us. He apparently heard the news today," a spokeswoman for Erato films told Reuters.
It was not known whether the film producer would be flying to Ireland. "Don't ask more, we are in shock," a spokeswoman for Unifrance said.
